items.text: An environmental activist in Kermanshah reported in a video on social media about planting about 50 kilograms of oak seeds in nature in memory of the martyrs. He said these seeds were planted for the Zagros and dedicated this action to the deceased and "homeland fighters."

Mojtaba Yousefi, a representative from Ahvaz in the parliament, said that in the next war, the economic interests of the US, US bases in Europe and the region, and infrastructures cooperating with the US will be legitimate targets. He also stated that trusting the US is futile and the damages from the 40-day war to the US are irreparable. Yousefi commented on the land blockade by some countries, saying if neighbors act according to Trump's views, Iran has the necessary means to respond.

The United States Congress has entered a new phase of investigations into the relationship between Gianni Infantino, FIFA president, and Donald Trump. These investigations include controversial cases such as the sale of World Cup shares and the pardon of a red card for a US national team star. Congress intends to investigate the possibility of a secret and illegal deal between Infantino and the Trump administration.

Meysam Nazari and Sobhan Amri, two detainees from the protest gathering on 26 Aban in Abdanan, were transferred to Ilam prison after completing interrogation stages at the Ilam Intelligence Department detention center.

Wynet reported that Roman Gofman, head of Mossad, supports a unilateral Israeli attack on the Islamic Republic, even without US participation if necessary. Israeli officials see the period leading up to the new US Congress session in early January as a potential opportunity for military action. Eyal Zamir, head of the Israeli army staff, believes the threat is not yet immediate and prefers to wait for Donald Trump's approval for joint military operations with the US.

Messages received by Iran International's Mediabat indicate non-payment of wages and insurance rights for workers in some production units. Workers at the Firouzabad Sodium Carbonate Company went on strike in protest of delayed wages. A worker at the Qazvin Glass Factory also reported several months of unpaid wages and insurance payments made only for three months from the beginning of the year.
A received video shows that a protesting citizen wrote slogans such as "Long live the Shah" and "Biji (Long live) Abdanan" on the walls of the Astara border regiment barracks.

Sohrab Bakhtiari-Zadeh, head coach of Esteghlal football team, praised his players' performance in Asia before their match against Sanat Naft Abadan in the 14th week of the Premier League and warned about the danger of negligence in the league. He emphasized the importance of the three points in this match and asked his players to be fully focused. Bakhtiari-Zadeh also mentioned the absence of three players and expressed confidence in the quality of the other players.

Shahram Irani, commander of the Navy of the Islamic Republic Army, said the enemy is mistaken and his comrades are waiting for the command to enter the scene. He added that the enemy has not been able to pass a vessel through the Strait of Hormuz and the order to keep the strait closed has been issued. Irani also said they will take revenge for the enemy's actions.

A severe storm swept through the eastern United States on Thursday, the fifth of Azar, coinciding with Thanksgiving. Wind speeds reached 113 kilometers per hour in some areas, trees were uprooted, and hundreds of thousands faced power outages. Heavy rain and strong winds also affected the streets of Midtown Manhattan in New York, making travel difficult.

Ali Abdollahi, Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces and Commander of the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, stated that the Navy is ready to give a decisive, effective, and regretful response to any threat or aggression from the enemy. He added that the armed forces have thwarted enemy plans with steadfastness and power. Abdollahi also said that the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz have become the center of strategic confrontation with the global arrogance front and Israel.

Vahid Shari'at, head of the Iranian Psychiatric Association, said about the new wave of alcohol poisoning that intentional alcohol poisoning, lack of effective drugs, and absence of serious harm reduction approaches are challenges. He added that intentional poisoning occurs for various reasons such as profiteering. Shari'at also said that toxic alcohol consumption can cause blindness and death, and most of its complications are preventable.

Recep Tayyip Erdogan, President of Turkey, officially confirmed the joint defense agreement of Mecca among Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia. According to this agreement, an attack on any one of the three countries is considered an attack on all of them. Pakistan will host a meeting of political and military officials from the three countries to discuss defense coordination and regional developments.

Shahram Irani, commander of the Navy of the Islamic Republic Army, said that on the first day of the war, his comrades identified the aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln and launched their first untested missile at it, which hit the target. He added that the enemy sought help from neighboring countries' ports to transfer wounded soldiers and continue its combat flights. He also said the enemy, despite its capabilities, is trapped in the Strait of Hormuz and has not been able to pass a single vessel through it.

Sirus Pourmousavi considered the absence of key Esteghlal players a good opportunity and expressed hope that his team would leave the field with full hands relying on their improving form. He praised Esteghlal's Asian performance and said his players are trying their best to move away from the bottom of the table. Pourmousavi referred to the absence of Yaser Asani and Aref Aghasi, saying Asani's absence might be an opportunity to exploit.

Hamidreza Haji Babaei, the parliament's deputy speaker, said that people may be dissatisfied with economic conditions but should not surrender to the enemy and must stand on the side of truth. He added that today people firmly stand behind the leadership, and this support shows the strength of the Islamic Republic. He also stated that the US and Israel face difficulties in decision-making about Iran, and the Islamic Republic continues to stand firm on its positions.

Sepehr Shokri's father asked Iranians worldwide to observe two minutes of silence every year on the nights of 18 and 19 Dey at 9 PM in honor of the victims. He also called for these two nights to be registered in the Iranian calendar so future generations know what crime happened against the youth. Sepehr Shokri, a 25-year-old, was killed by suppressors in Tehran on 18 Dey 1404.

Heavy rain and widespread flooding on Thursday, 5 Azar, in the city of Piura in northern Peru turned streets into rivers. Buildings were submerged and vehicles were trapped in the flood. Areas around the city's historic center, the Castillio market, and the Plaza Tres Culturas were also affected by the flooding.

Storm and strong winds in the US canceled more than 400 flights and delayed about 1,800 other flights. These storms also caused damage to buildings and power outages for hundreds of thousands of customers.

The case of Ilya Ben-Rashid, a protester sentenced to death during the nationwide protests of Dey 1404, has been referred to the Supreme Court. This prisoner is currently held in Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan. His death sentence was issued on charges of waging war and damaging public property.

Ahmad Khatami, Tehran's Friday prayer leader, said that the US has besieged Iran for 47 years but has not succeeded. He added that Iran has controlled the Strait of Hormuz for 9 months and the US is in a difficult situation. Khatami also emphasized the importance of economic mobilization to combat inflation and support the resistant economy, and described regional resistances as the fruit of the blessed tree.

Abdolnaser Hemmati, Governor of the Central Bank, wrote amid the record-breaking exchange rate in Iran's free market that no economic explanation or political consideration reduces their responsibility towards people's livelihood. He stated that maximum sanctions, military blockade, and restricted access to resources affect the currency market and prices, and emphasized that attributing all problems to sanctions does not replace internal policy reforms. Hemmati also responded to the US Treasury Secretary's claim about the collapse of Iran's economy, saying there is a large gap between the political desires of the sanctioners and the reality of Iran's economy.

Ebrahim Azizi, head of the Parliament's National Security Commission, reacted on Friday, 6 Azar, to the joint statement by Qatar and Germany against the Islamic Republic, saying that mediators should follow their role within the framework of mediation and should not enter into equations beyond what has been accepted as mediation. He added that if mediators present views or proposals outside the framework declared by the Islamic Republic, such positions will not be accepted. Azizi also said that Germans should recall their dark history when commenting on issues like human rights.

According to CNN, five female Argentine football players have filed a new complaint with FIFA accusing Diego Guacci, former coach of River Plate teams and national youth teams, of sexual harassment, threats, and psychological abuse. Florencia Mercau, a 32-year-old player, said Guacci sent her messages requesting nude photos shortly after she joined River Plate. Mercau also reported violent threats from Guacci.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Islamic Republic's claim of having no role in the drone attacks on Kuwait is not acceptable to the international community. He emphasized that the killing of two Italian nationals in these attacks could strengthen the political and military cooperation of European countries against the Islamic Republic.

Reports received by Iran International indicate that with the worsening economic conditions of the government, military personnel and their families have faced financial hardship. The wife of a military member stated that her husband's card balance is less than two million tomans. Additionally, a pensioner from Isfahan said that with a 32 million toman income and high expenses, she cannot manage to live.

Ahmad Alamolhoda, Khamenei's representative in Khorasan and Friday prayer leader of Mashhad, denied agreeing with Pezeshkian on holding Alireza Ghorbani's concert in the province and called it a rumor spread by "some wicked scoundrels and profiteering brokers." He said social and cultural issues are significant enough that he would not compromise on a program that disrespects the eighth Shia Imam. These remarks came after the public prosecutor of Khorasan Razavi also denied issuing a permit for the event.
The head of the Sardasht district court in Dezful reported the arrest of a person who was seen in a video assaulting a student in one of the schools in this county.

A video released on social media shows that Mohammad Parsa Amini's sister said at the commemoration ceremony of his birthday held at his grave that her brother was thinking of others' lives even in his last moments. Mohammad Parsa was killed in Dey 1404 while helping an injured protester at the age of 17.

Abdolnabi Mousavi-Fard, the representative of the Supreme Leader in Khuzestan and Friday prayer leader of Ahvaz, said that the Islamic Republic's armed forces dealt a blow to the US that destroyed Trump's reputation in Europe and worldwide. He added that the American people do not support Trump and ridicule him. Mousavi-Fard also said that the people and fighters of Iran have not retreated and have destroyed enemy bases.

Reuters reported on Friday, 6 Azar, citing three informed sources, that hackers have infiltrated the main cloud computing platform of the US Air Force. The breach was discovered about a month ago during efforts to upgrade the 'Cloud One' system. Inspectors from US Cyber Command have been asked to assess the damage caused by this attack.

Lotfollah Dejkam, the representative of the Supreme Leader in Fars province, said in the Friday prayer sermon in Shiraz that we must have resilience and not yield to enemy pressure. He added that we should see ourselves at the summit and strive to reach it. Dejkam also said that the US is in decline and its foundations of greatness are breaking.

Clashes between Olympique Marseille and Levski Sofia fans before the Europa League match took on political dimensions with strong reactions from the leaders of both countries. Emmanuel Macron emphasized the definite punishment of those responsible for the violence in talks with the Bulgarian Prime Minister. The Bulgarian Foreign Ministry called for a comprehensive investigation into the incident.

A video released shows the mother of Yousef Seyed Hosseini decorating his grave with flowers after the installation of his tombstone. Yousef, 20 years old, was killed on 19 Dey 1404 during the Parand protests in Tehran.

Javad Nekounam, Tractor's head coach, stated before the match against Zob Ahan that the main goal of his team is to earn 3 points to stay in the championship race. He explained about the defeat against Al Wasl and the condition of two of his players, saying both are healthy and Maria Jafari is ready to play. Nekounam also pointed to tactical changes by Zob Ahan and said his team's focus is on their own performance.

Abdulrahman Dawood, a Syrian journalist, said Syrian authorities have not shown much public reaction to the closure of two unofficial crossings between northeastern Syria and the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Syrian Kurdish parties have condemned this decision, and protests have been held in several areas. Some protesters have said they want to hold gatherings in Europe as well.

Reza Ebrahimpour Hargelan, a resident of Azarshahr, was arrested on Tuesday, the 2nd of Azar, in the city of Ilkhchi and transferred to an unknown location. After his arrest, his family was asked to collect his personal car from the Ilkhchi police station but received no information about his condition. Officials from the Azarshahr Intelligence Office stated that he was transferred to Tabriz and would contact his family, but no contact has been made so far.

In the second war between the US and Israel against the Islamic Republic, which began on 9 Esfand 1404 and ended with a ceasefire in Farvardin 1405, attacks on railway and road bridges became a prominent tactic that continued even after the ceasefire. Amirhadi Anvari from Iran International reported on the dual function of Iran's railway and road network. The report examines the potential military use of these routes by analyzing the locations of missile cities, missile industrial centers, and ground forces bases of the army and the IRGC.

The news website Ynet reported on Friday, 6 Azar, that remnants of an Iranian cluster bomb were found in a forested area in Sharon, Israel. Israeli police bomb disposal experts were dispatched to the site. Human Rights Watch had previously condemned the repeated use of cluster munitions by the Islamic Republic in attacks on densely populated areas of Israel.
A video published on social media shows a group of citizens in the west of Hormozgan province dancing in front of a wall with the slogan "Long live the Shah" written on it.

Marc Marquez, the Spanish motorcycle legend and eight-time MotoGP champion, announced his retirement at the end of the 2026 season. He stated that the Valencia Grand Prix will be his last professional race. This announcement was made during the live broadcast of the first practice session by raising cards in the style of the movie "Love Actually."

The Israeli army announced on Thursday that its fighter jets targeted Hezbollah positions in the Beqaa Valley in eastern Lebanon. Israel said Hezbollah intended to use these weapons to attack Israeli soldiers and civilians. Some media reported that Hezbollah is trying to rebuild and strengthen its military capabilities.

Ata Mohamad, an international relations expert, said that even if Tehran's direct role in the drone attack on Kuwait is not confirmed, reports about the drones being made in Iran could have political consequences for the Islamic Republic. He also considered the different accusations against Israel and Ukraine as a sign of confusion in the Islamic Republic's response.

Reuters reported on Friday, 6 Azar, that the operational unit of the Norwegian airline Norwegian North Atlantic declared bankruptcy due to a sharp increase in fuel costs caused by the Iran war. According to the report, the increase in fuel costs has put this low-cost airline in a financial crisis. Norwegian North Atlantic suspended all its flights on Thursday, 5 Azar.

Kuwait's Foreign Ministry summoned Mohammad Toutounchi, Iran's ambassador, on Friday, 6 Azar, and handed him a protest note regarding continued attacks by the Islamic Republic on Kuwait, including a drone attack on Thursday on one of the country's vital facilities. Kuwait's Deputy Foreign Minister described these attacks as a clear violation of Kuwait's sovereignty, international laws, the UN Charter, and Security Council Resolution 2817, holding the Islamic Republic responsible for all consequences. Kuwait's military had announced that two Italian citizens were killed in these attacks.

A video shows that family, friends, and some people in Kermanshah commemorated the birthday of Tiam Kianimansh in the Golestan neighborhood of the city. Tiam Kianimansh was shot and killed on 18 Dey during protests.

Some members of the Swedish Democrats party have submitted a proposal to the Swedish parliament calling for the expansion of targeted sanctions against officials of the Islamic Republic and their close relatives, including their children. These members also called for coordination of sanctions with the European Union and the United States, support for Iranian protesters, and countering the intelligence activities of the Islamic Republic on Swedish soil. This proposal has not yet been finally approved.
Mohammad Mokhber said that definitely neither the Strait of Hormuz will be opened nor will they allow the US naval blockade to remain closed. He added that this situation is happening right now.

The Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting news agency reported that following the death of two male students in Sirjan and increased concerns about the spread of respiratory diseases, schools in Sirjan County were made non-attendance starting Saturday, 7 Azar. Majid Esfandyarpour, the director of education in Sirjan, said that some students have severe colds or acute influenza, have been hospitalized at home, and are prohibited from attending school.

Mostafa Danandeh wrote that conscripted soldiers are vulnerable due to limited training and military unpreparedness in modern wars based on advanced technologies. He questioned whether it is realistic to expect these soldiers to perform like trained forces and who is responsible for the consequences. Today's wars, using new technologies such as drones and electronic warfare, require specialized training and high readiness.

A small number of Persepolis fans at Arak Stadium chanted "Have shame, let go" against Mehdi Tartaar, the coach of the Reds, at the end of their match against Aluminium in the fifteenth week. Persepolis drew 1-1 against Aluminium in Arak in the fifteenth week, placing second in the table due to fewer goals scored compared to Sepahan. Persepolis under Mehdi Tartaar remains unsuccessful in defeating top-half teams in the Premier League.

Mehdi Tartaar, Persepolis coach, said after the match that the game was not bad and his team had possession. He added that they were the better team but Aluminium's tight defense limited space and due to lack of focus, the opponent got a penalty. Tartaar said about fans' protests that they are dear to the team and much effort was made.

Maziar Zare, head coach of Malavan Bandar Anzali, resigned again after his team lost to Esteghlal Khuzestan. He said he had a meeting with the club owner three days ago and had decided to resign after this match regardless of the result. Zare had also resigned in previous weeks, but club officials opposed it and he returned to the team.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing a 23 million toman invoice for repairing his television and criticized the increase in home appliance repair costs. He said he bought this television about a year and a half ago for 35 million toman and now paid 23 million toman just to replace the lamps.

Hassan Mohammadian, the managing director of the news site "Didarnews," and Parvaneh Salahshouri, a former member of parliament, were each sentenced by Branch 8 of the Criminal Court One of Tehran Province to one year of suspended imprisonment and two years of prohibition from media activity.
A report states that Ahad Ardam and Mohammad Sarfejooei, citizens of Mahabad, were arrested on Sunday, 1 Azar, by intelligence officers in this city. Their place of detention is currently unknown.

Fouad Pashaei, Secretary General of the Constitutional Party of Iran, said the Iranian government targeted its opponents since coming to power and assassinated more than 320 of them in various countries until the Mykonos assassination. He added that after the judicial pursuit of the Mykonos case in Germany, the Islamic Republic changed its approach to opponents and increasingly resorted to accusations and defamation.
A firefighter was injured on Friday, 6 Azar, during a rescue operation of a mother and child from a fire at a scrap warehouse in Mashhad and was transferred to the hospital.
Videos received from Shahr-e Kord show graffiti with the slogans "Long live the Shah" and "Rise Iran".

Jürgen Hart, a member of the German Federal Parliament, announced that he has taken political sponsorship of Varisheh Moradi, a political prisoner sentenced to death. Hart stated his goal is to draw public attention to Moradi's case and increase pressure on the Islamic Republic authorities. Varisheh Moradi was sentenced to death on charges of "membership in a rebellious group."
Yesterday, Fatemeh (Mojgan) Tadrisi, a political prisoner held in Karaj's Kachouyi prison, was granted leave. This leave started on Thursday, 5 Azar, for a duration of three days.

Antonio Guterres, the UN Secretary-General, condemned the drone attack on Kuwait on Friday, 6 Azar, which resulted in the deaths of two Italian citizens and injuries to a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani citizen, and called on all parties to exercise restraint. Stephane Dujarric, the spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General, said Guterres expressed deep concern over escalating tensions in the region and called for refraining from any actions that would endanger regional peace and security. He also warned that the resumption of hostilities would have devastating consequences for the region and beyond.

A young man from Bandar-e-Gaz in Golestan province, who was sentenced to death for killing his friend during a fight, was released from execution due to the forgiveness of the victim's family. His case was scheduled for execution.
A viewer sent a video to Iran International showing that on the 6th of Azar, a queue of trucks and heavy vehicles formed in front of a diesel station in Shiraz.

In the past week, reports covered illegal hunting, air pollution especially in Khuzestan, forest fires in Gilan and Mazandaran, water resource depletion, land subsidence, and closure of polluting units. According to Harana News Agency, 13 flamingos died after hitting power cables in Tabas, and a new family of Asiatic cheetahs was identified. There were also reports of arrests and identification of hunters and wood traffickers, unhealthy air recorded in Khuzestan cities, pollution in Tehran, Isfahan, Mashhad, and Bushehr, forest fires in the Hyrcanian forests, and subsidence in Qazvin and Razavi Khorasan.

The public and revolutionary prosecutor of Ardakan announced the order to seal two commercial units and issue a warning to another unit in the city. Failure to comply with mandatory hijab was among the reasons cited for action against these commercial units.

The Khatoon Bam women's football team reduced their gap to league leader Persepolis to one point by winning 3-0 against Ilam Gas Refining in a postponed Premier League match. Marzieh Jafari's team reached 20 points and stood second in the table with one game less. Sepahan defeated Avaye Tehran 2-1 and climbed to fourth place in the standings.

Mohammad Taghavi said in the Hat-trick program about the match between Aluminium Arak and Persepolis: "Persepolis does not know all the ways to achieve victory. Persepolis fans are not satisfied with the team's condition and last year they did not give Vahid Hashemian a chance."

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing several grounded airplanes at Tehran's Khomeini Airport. The sender criticized the aviation fleet's condition, citing sanctions and parts shortages, saying: "We have neither parts, nor does anyone come or go."

Mehdi Nasiri, a political analyst, said Donald Trump still hopes that a faction within the Islamic Republic will emerge to negotiate with the US and reach an agreement leading to the government's surrender. He believes that some officials and commanders of the Islamic Republic communicating with the US and Israel could be a sign of efforts to prepare for the post-Islamic Republic era.

Masoud Sharifi, Deputy of Health Affairs at Sadoughi University of Medical Sciences in Yazd, announced that in the week ending on 6 Azar, over 30% of influenza tests among respiratory patients in this province were positive. He emphasized the need to increase preventive care and follow health recommendations. Sharifi said that pregnant women, the elderly, children, people with weakened immune systems, and those with chronic diseases are more at risk of severe illness and complications.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations Center announced that it received a report from military officials about an incident involving a cargo ship and military forces in the Sea of Oman on the 5th of Azar. Investigations into the incident are ongoing, and details, including the ship's name and the identity of the involved military forces, have not been disclosed.

Fatemeh Pasandideh, former Iranian women's national football player who sought asylum in Australia during the Asian Cup, spoke about the restrictions on women's football in Iran in response to Farideh Shojaei's remarks on mandatory hijab and gender discrimination. This was discussed in a conversation between Mazdak Mirzaei, Mohammad Taghavi, and Raha Pourbakhsh on the Hat-trick program.

In the continuation of the 14th week of the Premier League, Esteghlal will face Sanat Naft Abadan, Sepahan will play against Nassaji, and Tractor will face Zob Ahan. An interview with Mohammad Taghavi and Raha Pourbakhsh was conducted in the Hat-trick program.

A video released on social media shows a performance of Ashiq music at the grave of Arshia Emamgholizadeh Alamdari on his fourth anniversary; the 16-year-old Jolfan resident who was arrested due to "turban throwing" in the "Woman, Life, Freedom" uprising.

The Iranian Cinema Directors Association condemned the issuance and execution of harsh sentences against artists and called for an end to judicial actions and restrictions against them. The association supported the protest statement of the Iranian House of Music regarding the flogging sentence of Parastoo Ahmadi and emphasized the right of women to professional activity in music. It also cited the prison sentence and asset seizure of Jafar Panahi as an example of this concerning judicial trend.

The US State Department announced that the Islamic Republic has intensified transnational repression by using fabricated charges, confiscating opponents' assets, and pressuring their families. Simultaneously, CNN reported the transfer of six senior Trump administration officials to secure military residences following increased threats.

The Navy of the IRGC announced that a violating oil tanker exploded and caught fire after hitting a naval mine at the entrance of Khasab port, and another oil tanker exploded and caught fire on an unauthorized route east of the Strait of Hormuz. These tankers intended to secretly pass through the fake route of the Strait of Hormuz by turning off their positioning systems. The IRGC Navy stated that the fake route of the Strait of Hormuz is contaminated with very destructive mines, and US Army air support for the tankers will not save them from hitting mines.

Hossein Nejat, deputy commander of the IRGC at the Tharallah headquarters, described the country's security situation as very good and warned enemies that if they intend to create insecurity, they can test the power of the Iranian government. He said the enemy does not have the ability to create insecurity and dozens of armed gangs have been arrested so far.

The office of Prince Reza Pahlavi announced gatherings and memorial ceremonies on the 18th and 19th of Dey to commemorate those who died in the Dey protests. These events coincide with the first anniversary of what the office called the "National Uprising of the Lion and Sun of Iran." More details will be announced after the plans are finalized.

The International Institute for Strategic Studies has reported the expansion and change in the pattern of the Islamic Republic's intelligence and sabotage operations in Europe. According to the report, since the war began in Esfand last year, Jewish centers, commercial interests, and military facilities hosting American forces have been especially targeted. The institute has monitored 80 operations linked to the IRGC or other intelligence agents of the Islamic Republic, with only 58% leading to arrests.

The Iran Human Rights Organization expressed serious concern about the physical condition of Mahdi Mahmoudian, a detained journalist and human rights activist, and called for his immediate and unconditional release. Mahmoudian was arrested on Wednesday and severely beaten and tortured at the security police, then transferred to a hospital and after a few hours returned to Tehran's Great Prison. The organization demanded Mahmoudian's immediate access to independent medical services, forensic examination, and unrestricted access to his chosen lawyer.

Meysam Mehrani, a political analyst, said that the defense pact between Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan is unlikely to lead to a joint military action against the Houthis in practice; because Ankara and Islamabad do not want to jeopardize their relations with the Islamic Republic.

Molavi Abdolhamid, Sunni Friday prayer leader of Zahedan, said at Friday prayers that implementing justice and respecting people's rights guarantee the security and peace of nations, adding that no individual or government has the right to oppress others. He emphasized that justice and fairness establish security, while oppression makes the world unsafe. He also stated that governments responsible for managing society must uphold justice and ensure the rights of all individuals are protected.

Reza Amiri-Moghaddam, Iran's ambassador to Pakistan, said messages are exchanged between Iran and the United States through Qatar and Pakistan, and talks with the American side continue. He added Tehran is ready to negotiate but will respond decisively if attacked. Regarding China's initiative to resolve the Yemen crisis, he said China and Russia consider the Houthis a reality and Iran welcomes engagement with them.

The Israeli army announced that it killed two members of Hamas's military wing who were operating under the cover of humanitarian activities in an attack in Gaza City. These individuals were reportedly planning attacks on civilians and Israeli forces while simultaneously serving as guards at a clinic managed by Doctors Without Borders. Doctors Without Borders confirmed the deaths of their two guards and called for accountability from those responsible for the attack.

The Washington Post reported that damages from missile and drone attacks by the Islamic Republic on the US Navy support base in Bahrain will likely exceed $400 million. The Pentagon is considering relocating its forces from the region to Israel and Jordan. The Bahraini government confirmed its strategic cooperation with the US but declined to comment on the base's future.

Shahram Kholdi said Donald Trump is buying time by continuing message exchanges and giving a one-month opportunity to the Islamic Republic. He added that the Trump administration must decide between continuing the status of neither war nor peace, entering war, or reaching an understanding.

Farzin Nadimi, a senior defense and security researcher, says the deployment of special forces, drones, and artillery of the IRGC in western Iran indicates the execution of a coordinated counter-guerrilla and anti-riot operation. He said this operation covers several provinces from West Azerbaijan to Kermanshah, and the increased military presence of the IRGC in border areas shows the government's concern about armed Kurdish groups.

Simultaneous with the spread of the flu wave in Iran, two children in Sirjan died due to this disease. The head of the Iranian Infectious Disease Specialists Association stated that the flu prevalence has exceeded 20 percent, and about half of the positive cases are among individuals under 15 years old. Nezamoddin Misaghi explained the difference of this year's flu wave compared to previous years and the role of delayed medical visits in increasing severe cases and mortality.

Sadegh Beigdeli said the Islamic Republic is trying to buy time for a potential confrontation with the US and Israel while continuing message exchanges and expanding military and security activities. He added that the Medicalian government plays the role of the "good cop" and the hard core of power plays the "bad cop," both acting to preserve the Islamic Republic.

On the eve of the 2026 Nobel Prize ceremony, Stockholm hosted a fashion show featuring an Iranian designer. At this show, a collection of clothes was unveiled that this Iranian artist designed for some special guests of the Nobel ceremony.

Hossein Shariatmadari, the Supreme Leader's representative in Kayhan newspaper, wrote that a retaliatory attack on the oil and gas facilities of Arab countries allied with the US in the Persian Gulf could be a way to counter the naval blockade. He added that this action is legal and part of the war and questioned why this leverage should not be used. Shariatmadari also pointed to the inconsistency of Arab countries' cooperation with the US and Israel in attacking Iran.

On the eve of the first anniversary of the Iranian National Revolution, calls have been made to turn the commemoration of the immortalized into a global movement aimed at recording the truth and seeking justice. Pegah Bani Hashemi, a senior legal researcher, explains ways to turn this collective movement into effective pressure on international institutions to prosecute those responsible for the January massacre.

Jalal Ejadi, a sociology professor, said that despite the identification and arrest of agents involved in sabotage operations attributed to the Islamic Republic in Europe, these actions have not yet led to deterrence. He considers concerns about hostage-taking and the activities of secret networks of the Islamic Republic among the factors preventing a decisive reaction from European countries. He emphasizes the necessity of security cooperation and practical action by Europe against Tehran's threats.

Financial Times reported, citing informed sources, that about six drones were observed in early November over Lakenheath Air Base in eastern Britain. American anti-drone systems managed to repel them, but British and American forces could not recover them. The possibility of the Islamic Republic's connection to this incident is under investigation.

Shahram Irani, commander of the Navy of the Islamic Republic Army, said in a TV program that multiple operations are ahead and their ultimate goal is to expel enemies from the West Asia region and the Indian Ocean area. He added that the blockade the enemies mention is actually a self-blockade and the Navy of the Islamic Republic has not blockaded them.

Mohammad Mirzaei, a member of the Parliament's Cultural Commission, said there were plans to reduce the Shia population because he believes Shias threaten imperialist interests. He added that Shia children defend their homeland and special measures must be taken to neutralize these policies.

Kiumars Heydari, deputy chief of staff of the Islamic Republic's armed forces, said Iran no longer has geographical limitations in responding to enemy actions and any threat against Iran will be targeted. He also stated that the armed forces are in absolute readiness to respond to the "enemy's mistake" and do not pay attention to Trump's timing for his actions.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, said on Saturday, 7 Azar, that the enemy is trying to fuel protests and social problems by creating shortages. He asked people to help frustrate the enemy by preventing waste of resources such as gas, electricity, gasoline, and diesel. Pezeshkian added that people's cooperation will defeat the enemy and they will manage the winter without cuts in electricity, gas, gasoline, and other fuels needed for production.
